units.translation: [Ch. 536 ἀνῆλθον [went up] corrupt from ἀνῆθον [bloomed]. See ἀναίθω.]
But when the bright light of the sun had risen.
without chariots and the former luxury
whose murder he will discover (thus Porson for ἂν εὐρήσῃ)
i.e. holding the ear upward, as the grammarians cited in the note explain.
Thus Jacobs for ηύχετο [prayed], which is in Athenaeus 7 p. 303 c.
For we endured many former evils.
But never yet have I endured such a calamity.
Of the glorious contests of the slain I will not endure not to honor this city, victorious among mortals.
Will you not endure these things in silence to your ruin?
For I know that she will endure hearing from you alone.
And being called a wanderer I endured.
Who, like a tunny, endured without groaning, speechless.
one might say that there is some accomplishment.
O death, healer, for you alone are the physician of incurable evils.
But how is it possible to disobey the words of your father?
(Doric ἀνάλιος) lacking the light of the sun
in the sunless recesses of caves
the sunless, all-receiving land to the unseen
with sunless (thus I wrote for ἀνηλίῳ) torch
For they are savage and not approachable to strangers.
making the land savage that had been tamed
eaters of the savage spears of seeds
Of a man insofar as he has a wife

[from a short vowel, but lengthened in epic and lyric forms ἀνέρος ἀνέρι ἀνέρα ἀνέρες ἀνέρων ἀνέρας [of a man, to a man, a man, men, of men, men], which the tragedians sometimes used in lyric passages. Aeschylus has one example in a cretic verse Suppl. 426 γνῶθι δ᾽ ὕβριν ἀνέρων [know the insolence of men].]
Thus I corrected what is read in M: οὔποτε τὰν Διὸς ἁρμονίαν θνατῶν παρεξίασι βουλαί [never will the counsels of mortals transgress the harmony of Zeus].
where I restored ἀνδρῶν [of men] for ανοσ (i.e. ἄνθρωπος [human]), which is in M, changed by a corrector to ἄλλος [other].
Of a man insofar as he is opposed to a woman
I say to honor me as a man, not as a god.
objects of hatred for men and Olympian gods
never will the counsels of men transgress the harmony of Zeus
never will the counsels of mortals transgress the harmony of Zeus
so that neither any of the gods nor any of men rejoiced at these things,
man and woman and whatever is between them
For it is a concern for a man; let not a woman plan.
not of a man, not of a woman.
